Evidence Summary: C3 AI agents execute multi-step database queries, analyze information, surface insights, and orchestrate enterprise workflows autonomously. They dynamically generate and run Python scripts in real time while leveraging error self-correction and reflection mechanisms to refine outputs without manual intervention.
Evaluation Notes: Uses automated reflection loops, tool selection, and dynamic script generation to execute multi-step workflows against enterprise systems.

Evidence Summary: Employs an evaluation framework with three feedback loops (automated ML metrics, ground-truth comparison, LLM self-grading with human calibration). The STAFF framework distills operational history into fine-tuned agents, while few-shot examples guide in-context adaptation.
Evaluation Notes: Combines three-tiered evaluation loops and agent distillation with configurable in-context few-shot learning.

Evidence Summary: Uses vector-store RAG combined with long-term memory to maintain domain-specific context, atomic tasks, and few-shot examples. Short-term conversational context is preserved within active and recent user sessions.
Evaluation Notes: Merges vector retrieval with persistent few-shot example memory. Public docs emphasize session-level context, while persistent long-term memory leverages domain stores.

Evidence Summary: Dynamic multi-hop orchestration agents utilize step-by-step reasoning (inspired by Demonstrate-Search-Predict / Read-Extract-Answer frameworks) to interpret queries, select tools, retrieve context, and execute tasks across multiple iterative hops.
Evaluation Notes: Supports iterative multi-step reasoning, dynamic tool selection, and context retrieval over complex, heterogeneous data.

Evidence Summary: C3 Agentic AI Platform provides Agentic Process Automation (APA) and Agentic Workflows over C3 AI Object Models. It connects data sources, ML models, and business logic into directed graph workflows and self-executing decision chains triggered on schedule, on demand, or by data events.
Evaluation Notes: Enables graph-based workflow definition, scheduled/event-driven task orchestration, and structured data retrieval pipelines.

Evidence Summary: C3 AI Studio provides a graphical Application Canvas and visual UI where users can construct dashboards, configure workflows, management/delete, and interactively test agents using natural language or by cloning templates (e.g., Dynamic, Canvas, Deep Research agents).
Evaluation Notes: Features low-code Application Canvas, template duplication, and visual data pipeline design tools.

Evidence Summary: Features C3 Code (a natural-language development environment), native VS Code extensions, managed JupyterLab services with pre-written code blocks, pre-built domain templates, and reusable tools/components to streamline agent development.
Evaluation Notes: Comprehensive developer tooling combining visual low-code managers with IDE extensions and sample code libraries.

Evidence Summary: Standardized LLM client interface supports commercial models (Azure OpenAI, Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI/PaLM/Gemini, Claude), open-source models (Llama, Mistral, Falcon, FLAN-T5), and custom fine-tuned enterprise models without altering application logic.
Evaluation Notes: Allows switching underlying LLM providers and models seamlessly via a standardized client abstraction.

Evidence Summary: C3 AI's STAFF framework and C3 Generative AI architecture orchestrate specialized agents (process extraction, generators, critics, tool users) structured as directed graphs, using a central orchestrator to coordinate tools, models, and decision nodes.
Evaluation Notes: Multi-agent interaction is modeled as directed graph topologies of specialized agents coordinated via a central orchestrator.

Evidence Summary: Agents deploy as C3 AI-managed or customer-managed cloud services across AWS (including AWS GovCloud and ICMP Marketplace), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, or on-premises/air-gapped FedRAMP environments using Kubernetes (RKE2/OpenShift).
Evaluation Notes: Highly flexible deployment footprint supporting multicloud, hybrid, on-premises Kubernetes, and air-gapped government clouds.

Evidence Summary: C3 AI Studio, Data Fusion, and custom agent tools integrate with enterprise systems (SAP, ERP, CRM, SCADA, sensor data) using REST APIs, C3 AI Type System object models, pre-built connectors, and cloud storage/database access tools.
Evaluation Notes: Uses C3 Type System and Data Fusion visual connectors for seamless enterprise system integration.

Evidence Summary: Enforces multi-level authentication (OIDC, SAML, OAuth 2.0) and dynamic, programmatically settable row-level authorization for data objects/methods using RBAC, SOC/FedRAMP compliant audit trails, and config change auditing.
Evaluation Notes: Enterprise-grade security featuring row-level authorization, compliance audit logs, and modern SSO protocol support.

Evidence Summary: Supports interactive execution with human verification and approval checkpoints (e.g., turbine-monitoring workflows routing drafted work orders to schedulers for approval before execution).
Evaluation Notes: Built-in interactive checkpoints allow explicit human review steps within complex automated agent workflows.

Evidence Summary: Agent Workbench delivers execution trace visibility into reasoning chains and step-level callbacks. The platform provides source data citations, interactive chat verification, visual data lineage, model explainability, and config auditing (users, timestamps, actions).
Evaluation Notes: Combines exact source attribution and visual data lineage with operational trace visibility and configuration auditing.

Evidence Summary: Offers over 40 pre-built enterprise applications and generative AI solutions spanning Defense & Intelligence, Manufacturing, Utilities, Oil & Gas, Healthcare, Supply Chain, and Financial Services.
Evaluation Notes: Extensive pre-built operational applications and domain algorithms validated across diverse global industries.

Evidence Summary: Documented real-world impacts include US Marine Corps decision optimization, asset inspection acceleration, a 55% improvement in lead-time prediction for a global retailer, and a 2.8% revenue uplift for a contract manufacturer, with initial production deployment in 6 months.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates quantifiable customer ROI and operational improvements, though results are customer-reported.

Evidence Summary: Model-driven Type System architecture handles petabyte-scale data ingestion and manages operations from single models up to millions of deployed models, utilizing elastic compute, dedicated compute pools, and Kubernetes cluster orchestration to handle concurrent requests automatically.
Evaluation Notes: Scales automatically across Kubernetes infrastructure with dedicated compute pools and dev/test/prod environment isolation.

Evidence Summary: Google Cloud's Agent Platform enables agents to evaluate context, execute multi-step goals, run code in secure sandboxes, and determine tool usage autonomously. AES uses Claude on Vertex AI to automate auditing without constant monitoring.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Secure sandbox execution and proven autonomous decision-making.

Evidence Summary: Example Store and Gen AI Evaluation Service support performance monitoring and prompt refinement. Vertex AI also supports reinforcement-learning fine-tuning.
Evaluation Notes: Combines evaluation feedback with model-level reinforcement fine-tuning.

Evidence Summary: Agent Engine Memory Bank stores and manages long-term user information across sessions. Agent Platform Sessions manage short-term state.
Evaluation Notes: Supports memory extraction, consolidation, contradiction resolution, similarity search, and TTL expiration.

Evidence Summary: Vertex AI Reasoning Engine combines Gemini thinking models with agent frameworks for multi-step reasoning, ReAct loops, and dynamic tool selection. ADK supports planning and task decomposition.
Evaluation Notes: Native Gemini integration and custom Python support. Planning is an advanced capability and not enabled for all agent types by default.

Evidence Summary: Agent Designer and ADK support visual and programmatic orchestration using sequential, parallel, loop, and LLM-driven workflows.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Supports visual flow editing and complex multi-agent architectures.

Evidence Summary: Agent Designer provides natural-language interaction and visual workflows for creating, testing, and connecting agents to sources such as Gmail, Drive, and Jira.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Available across Gemini Enterprise editions and includes CX Agent Studio.

Evidence Summary: ADK enables production-ready agents with relatively little code and provides Agent Garden, CLI evaluation, and a visual Web UI for testing.
Evaluation Notes: Supports rapid prototyping through Google AI Studio, Cloud Shell, and local evaluation tools.

Evidence Summary: Supports Gemini, open-source models through Model Garden/Hugging Face, custom vLLM containers, and third-party models such as Claude, OpenAI, and Mistral.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Gemini has the deepest native support; other models may require LiteLLM or custom vLLM deployment.

Evidence Summary: ADK and the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol support heterogeneous agents discovering capabilities, delegating tasks, and collaborating across platforms.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: A2A enables cross-platform and cross-vendor agent interoperability.

Evidence Summary: Agents can run on Vertex AI Agent Engine, Cloud Run, GKE, Google Distributed Cloud (air-gapped), or custom infrastructure using Terraform.
Evaluation Notes: Supports managed, serverless, air-gapped, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code deployments.

Evidence Summary: Agents integrate through MCP, OpenAPI, Apigee API Hub, 100+ Application Integration connectors, and Google Search grounding.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Native MCP proxy support, enterprise connectors, and live grounding.

Evidence Summary: Features include Cloud IAM agent identity, Model Armor, VPC Service Controls, CMEK encryption, and Agent Registry governance.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Provides prompt-injection protection, least-privilege IAM, and audit controls.

Evidence Summary: Agent Builder and ADK allow workflows to pause for human approval, preserve execution state, rewind conversations, and enable operator review.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories; Official product documentation
Evaluation Notes: State checkpoints are maintained automatically during approval pauses.

Evidence Summary: Cloud Logging, Monitoring, Trace, and ADK OpenTelemetry conventions track execution logic, reasoning steps, and tool calls.
Evaluation Notes: Strong tracing and monitoring, but formal feature-attribution explainability is limited.

Evidence Summary: Google Cloud provides domain-specific platforms such as CX Agent Studio and documented deployments across finance, real estate, retail, legal, and customer support.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrated adoption across multiple enterprise domains.

Evidence Summary: Google Cloud customer deployments report measurable operational and financial benefits, including AES reducing audit costs by 99% and audit time from 14 days to one hour, Commerzbank reducing administration time by 66%, and Wayfair updating product attributes 4× faster with Vertex AI.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates operational value, although reported figures are self-reported by customers.

Evidence Summary: Managed Agent Runtime automatically scales compute, memory, and sessions. GKE supports horizontal pod autoscaling with GPU/TPU acceleration.
Evaluation Notes: Supports multi-region serverless deployments and high-throughput GKE workloads.

Evidence Summary: Glean Agents execute multi-step workflows autonomously—retrieving information, executing code, and triggering actions across enterprise tools based on conversational, scheduled, trigger-based, or form inputs. Scheduled/background agents can run headless end-to-end without per-run user confirmation.
Evaluation Notes: Autonomous tool invocation and headless background runs are subject to administrator and agent-permission controls.

Evidence Summary: Glean agents adapt dynamically during loops using tool feedback and intermediate results. Performance is continuously monitored via Agent Insights user feedback metrics (thumbs up/down), task-specific LLM judges, and evaluation test sets to guide prompt/step refinement.
Evaluation Notes: Evidence supports runtime loop adaptation and builder-driven prompt refinement based on analytics, but not autonomous continual model retraining from errors.

Evidence Summary: Agents store inputs, outputs, conversation history, and prior step results in memory, leveraging Glean's Enterprise Graph and semantic RAG to persist and retrieve permission-aware context across connected company sources. Sub-agent outputs return directly to parent agent memory.
Evaluation Notes: Combines real-time step execution memory with enterprise-wide graph retrieval. Memory primarily persists execution context rather than cross-session user memory across unrelated runs.

Evidence Summary: Glean's agentic planner breaks down complex goals using multi-stage prompting and prompt chaining, leveraging reasoning models (e.g., o3, Gemini Pro 2.5) to decide intermediate logic, select tools, and loop/branch until goal conditions are met.
Evaluation Notes: Supports reasoning-specific LLMs at both the overall agent level and individual step levels; adapts subsequent tool calls based on intermediate results.

Evidence Summary: Glean Agent Builder provides a visual flow canvas to define triggers, step sequences, document read actions, prompt formatting, loops, and conditional branching. Agents can also be auto-drafted from natural language and use planner-driven orchestration for multi-step execution and retries.
Evaluation Notes: Workflows support both visual step-by-step manual configuration and natural language generation.

Evidence Summary: Glean Agent Builder provides a no-code visual canvas and a conversational "Build with Natural Language" interface that automatically generates workflow steps, triggers, and tool configurations from plain text descriptions.
Evaluation Notes: Users can visually reorder steps, add branching, and configure tool parameters; natural language drafting requires an agentic model configured in the org.

Evidence Summary: Features natural-language workflow generation, prebuilt agent templates, action integrations, prompt enhancement, live draft previewing, and an interactive step-by-step debug mode to inspect raw tool inputs, outputs, and data transformations.
Evaluation Notes: Interactive debug mode and prebuilt templates significantly reduce custom development overhead.

Evidence Summary: Glean's Model Hub supports commercial and open-source models from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT-4, o3), Google (Gemini), Amazon, and Meta. Models can be configured globally, per agent, or independently for individual workflow steps.
Evaluation Notes: Allows granular, step-level assignment of specialized reasoning models versus standard generation models. Availability depends on hosting environment.

Evidence Summary: Glean supports Sub-agents as direct workflow steps (allowing parent agents to delegate tasks and ingest results) and enables agents to be exposed as callable tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway for external multi-agent systems.
Evaluation Notes: MCP gateway compatibility enables standard agent-to-agent tool invocation across internal workflows and external agent platforms.

Evidence Summary: Glean is available as a fully managed SaaS deployment or as Customer-Hosted Cloud-Prem in the customer's own AWS or GCP VPC environment, with support for private networking to on-prem data sources and AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMK).
Evaluation Notes: Cloud-Prem provides isolated customer cloud deployment rather than a traditional bare-metal/on-premise package.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides 100+ native connectors (GitHub, Jira, Salesforce, Slack, Google Workspace, M365, Snowflake, Zendesk), standard REST APIs, and remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/gateway support to connect custom external tools.
Evaluation Notes: Exposes Glean enterprise knowledge and actions via both standard REST APIs and MCP interfaces (remote MCP noted in Beta).

Evidence Summary: Features real-time enterprise permission mirroring (document-level ACLs), RBAC, SSO, administrator roles, audit logs, DLP policy enforcement, content-hiding APIs, SOC 2 Type II compliance, and granular publishing/background execution controls.
Evaluation Notes: Strict identity, access control, and automated governance violation enforcement across all integrated enterprise data.

Evidence Summary: Glean enforces confirmation panels for write actions in interactive web sessions (allowing users to review, edit planned changes inline, approve, or cancel) and provides a dedicated "Wait for User Input" action for human confirmation workflows.
Evaluation Notes: Applied by default to interactive write actions to prevent accidental or unauthorized data modifications.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides agent run history, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, step-level debug traces of tool payloads, deep-linked citations linking directly back to source documents, and an Agent Insights dashboard tracking adoption and user feedback.
Evaluation Notes: Strong operational observability and deep-linked source attribution; does not represent formal model feature-attribution explainability.

Evidence Summary: Glean provides pre-built workflows and action packs across HR, IT service management, software engineering, finance, legal/contracts, recruiting, customer support, and sales ops (with deployments at Zillow, Duolingo, DNI, and McCarthy).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Broad cross-industry coverage with specialized workflows for code search, ticket deflection, and CRM management.

Evidence Summary: A Forrester Total Economic Impact study found a 141% three-year ROI, payback in under 6 months, and $26.6M in total benefits for a 10k-employee firm (saving up to 110 hrs/employee annually); Duolingo reported a 5x ROI and $1.1M in annual time savings.
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates substantial productivity and time-saving gains; Forrester study was commissioned by Glean and customer metrics are self-reported.

Evidence Summary: Glean scales automatically across SaaS and isolated Cloud-Prem environments, processing petabyte-scale search and agent workloads using distributed indexing, KV cache optimization for latency, and scalable MCP architectures (e.g., 3,400+ agents deployed at Zillow).
Evaluation Notes: Verified enterprise adoption supporting thousands of concurrent users and agents across large-scale corp infrastructures.

Evidence Summary: K2view Data Agent Builder and AI Fusion enable autonomous agents to analyze incoming context, determine which enterprise data to retrieve, sequence actions, execute dynamic Python scripts, and select tools (text-to-SQL, APIs, data services, vector search) via an MCP orchestrator without manual intervention.
Evaluation Notes: Agents execute multi-step flows and utilize automated error-handling/reflection routines to construct context.

Evidence Summary: The AI Fusion Evaluation module provides multi-turn testing frameworks, LLM-as-judge scoring (accuracy, relevance, clarity), and continuous regression testing to evaluate and refine agent prompts/performance before deployment.
Evaluation Notes: Evaluated via pre-deployment benchmark scoring and regression testing; no official evidence of autonomous continual self-training from live production interactions.

Evidence Summary: K2view maintains real-time operational business context by organizing enterprise data into entity-based Micro-Databases (each customer/device maintains an isolated, always-fresh dataset) and vector stores. Its MCP orchestrator applies memory for multi-turn conversation continuity and session recall.
Evaluation Notes: Supports runtime continuity and persistent entity-level business context; does not provide a separate personal long-term memory engine.

Evidence Summary: Utilizes chain-of-thought prompt orchestration, prompt chaining, ReAct patterns, reflection, and schema-aware semantic query generation to break down complex user requests into discrete execution steps and SQL actions within an agentic RAG architecture.
Evaluation Notes: Supported by the platform's semantic enrichment, data grounding layer, and dynamic planning capabilities.

Evidence Summary: The Broadway orchestration engine coordinates multi-step business logic, data pipelines, and agent flows using configurable Stages and reusable modular Actors. K2view's MCP orchestrator plans processes, executes multi-stage data flows, and automates Data-as-a-Service delivery.
Evaluation Notes: Broadway flows can be nested, exported, and reused as discrete actors across pipelines.

Evidence Summary: K2view Data Agent Builder provides a low-code/no-code visual environment in K2studio, featuring drag-and-drop workflow assembly, prebuilt agent templates, AI-assisted data-product design, and over 200 prebuilt data-processing functions.
Evaluation Notes: Generally available visual no-code environment for rapid agent prototyping and deployment.

Evidence Summary: Provides a built-in chat playground, interactive visual debugging, step-by-step execution traces, live token and payload inspection, prebuilt agent templates, over 200 data functions, and centralized MCP connection setup via Studio AI.
Evaluation Notes: Accelerates testing and debugging by allowing real-time inspection of intermediate states, tokens, and data transformations.

Evidence Summary: Features an LLM-agnostic architecture with out-of-the-box connectors for commercial and open-source models (installed via K2exchange). K2view Studio AI allows administrators to assign different models to specific agents, set model aliases, and configure fallback priority lists.
Evaluation Notes: Centralized configuration interface supports multi-LLM routing, aliases, and connector updates.

Evidence Summary: Data Agent Builder and AI Fusion support multi-agent system design and orchestration within Broadway flows, allowing specialized sub-agents and tool-calling agents to collaborate, share context, and execute tasks across structured hierarchical pipelines.
Evaluation Notes: Organizes heterogeneous sub-agents into structured, hierarchical execution paths and collaborative workflows.

Evidence Summary: Supports cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), hybrid, on-premises, and multi-cloud deployment models. Deployments are managed across Kubernetes-orchestrated container environments (via K2cloud Orchestrator), supporting data-mesh and data-fabric topologies.
Evaluation Notes: Fully covers self-hosted Kubernetes, managed cloud spaces, hybrid networks, and air-gapped on-premises deployments.

Evidence Summary: Integrates with enterprise systems via Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP), REST/Web Service APIs, CDC, streaming message brokers, and native database connectors. Data products can expose governed business entity data directly as MCP tools.
Evaluation Notes: Native MCP server support allows LLMs to query databases, retrieve docs, and call enterprise APIs with governed context.

Evidence Summary: Data security is enforced through individually 256-bit encrypted Micro-Databases, dynamic on-the-fly data masking, role-based access control (RBAC), entity-level isolation boundaries (preventing cross-entity data leakage), and complete audit logging of agent operations.
Evaluation Notes: Entity-level isolation and dynamic masking ensure strict data privacy and regulatory compliance (SOC/GDPR/HIPAA-ready).

Evidence Summary: Supports human-in-the-loop controls within Broadway flows and task orchestration, enabling approval stages, role-scoped guided execution interfaces, parameter overrides, and manual review checkpoints before operations proceed.
Evaluation Notes: Administrators configure role-based approval steps and interactive checkpoints directly in data pipelines.

Evidence Summary: Observation Dashboard tracks agent activity, conversation pathways, token consumption, sentiment, satisfaction, resolution, and risk levels. AI Agent History logs requests, responses, and injected context with drill-down trace views into individual session steps.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers end-to-end operational observability, token tracking, and trace-level visibility (not formal model feature attribution).

Evidence Summary: Provides domain-specific data models and solutions for telecommunications, financial services, insurance, healthcare, and retail (e.g., Customer 360, billing inquiry automation, Customer Service Rep Assist).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Features prebuilt entity schemas and vertical customer service solutions deployed at major telcos like Cellcom and Pelephone.

Evidence Summary: Customer deployments (e.g., Cellcom, Pelephone) demonstrate operational impacts including shorter wait/handling times, higher first-contact resolution (FCR), reduced representative ramp-up time, and accelerated AI service rollout, with rapid initial production delivery.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates quantifiable operational benefits in customer support; metrics are customer-reported rather than independently audited.

Evidence Summary: Distributed Micro-Database architecture enables sub-second query retrieval and linearly scales across millions to billions of concurrent entities (over 4B Micro-Databases deployed; 7B+ requests served daily) handling petabyte-scale data on Kubernetes.
Evaluation Notes: Proven high-throughput scalability in tier-1 enterprise production environments.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce operates autonomously via the Atlas Reasoning Engine, analyzing incoming user queries or events, classifying intents under configured Topics, and independently selecting and executing actions (such as Salesforce Flows, Apex, prompt templates, or API calls) without scripted decision trees.
Evaluation Notes: Operates autonomously within configured Topic instructions, action targets, and guardrails to perform tasks rather than just generate responses.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce logs prompts, responses, and trust signals in Data 360/Data Cloud. The Agentforce Testing Center and Connect APIs provide automated evaluation suites, custom scoring criteria, and simulated testing in sandboxes to iteratively refine prompts, instructions, and Agent Scripts based on feedback.
Evaluation Notes: Supports iterative human-guided refinement and automated regression testing; does not represent autonomous continual model retraining from live production data.

Evidence Summary: Context assembly combines multi-turn conversational history (via Agent Script variables and dialogue state tracking) with real-time semantic grounding from Salesforce CRM and Data Cloud records across session turns.
Evaluation Notes: Evidence supports real-time CRM/Data Cloud grounding and session state memory; does not establish general-purpose persistent long-term memory across independent sessions.

Evidence Summary: The Atlas Reasoning Engine employs a ReAct-based planning and reasoning framework that translates complex user goals into step-wise execution plans, dynamically orchestrates tool invocations, and assesses intermediate outcomes, treating execution plans as living documents adjusted during multi-step reasoning.
Evaluation Notes: Combines LLM reasoning with deterministic logic via Agent Script and Atlas dynamic tool selection.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce orchestrates business workflows using modular building blocks (Topics, Instructions, and Actions) and Agent Script. It supports deterministic action chaining, conditional branching, subagent routing, transitions, and direct connections to Salesforce Flow, Apex classes, MuleSoft APIs, and external REST endpoints.
Evaluation Notes: Supports visual flow authoring in Flow Builder as well as programmatic script definitions.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce Builder provides a declarative low-code/no-code graphical interface and built-in AI assistance to define agent topics, assign actions, configure natural-language instructions, and preview/test responses interactively using clicks.
Evaluation Notes: Includes conversational prompt-based agent generation, prebuilt templates, and visual configuration tools.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce DX integrates with Salesforce CLI, Visual Studio Code extensions, Agent Script authoring, scratch orgs, visual Canvas, live draft previewing, and prebuilt reusable templates to streamline both pro-code and low-code agent creation and testing.
Evaluation Notes: Supports bi-directional synchronization between local developer projects and Salesforce orgs.

Evidence Summary: Einstein 1 Studio Model Builder supports Bring Your Own Large Language Model (BYOLLM) and an LLM Open Connector, allowing organizations to connect external foundation models (such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) alongside Salesforce-hosted models, assignable per agent or subagent.
Evaluation Notes: Requires Data Cloud enablement for external model registration and custom endpoint connections.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce supports multi-agent architectures where specialized agents, subagents, and connected subagents collaborate, share context, delegate domain-specific subtasks, and coordinate across distinct business workflows in the same Salesforce org.
Evaluation Notes: Connected-subagent multi-agent orchestration is documented as a Beta service.

Evidence Summary: Agents can be deployed across multiple channels (Salesforce Omni-Channel, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Slack, WhatsApp, SMS, mobile apps, web chat) and moved across sandbox, scratch, and production orgs via Agentforce DX metadata deployment.
Evaluation Notes: Supports multi-channel engagement managed via Salesforce metadata; does not support arbitrary self-hosted runtime deployment.

Evidence Summary: Agents connect to third-party tools and enterprise systems using MuleSoft Anypoint integration, Salesforce External Services via OpenAPI specifications, standard Apex classes, Flow HTTP callouts, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) solutions.
Evaluation Notes: Native MuleSoft ecosystem connectivity provides extensive enterprise API management and orchestration.

Evidence Summary: Executed natively within Salesforce Hyperforce, the Einstein Trust Layer enforces dynamic PII data masking, toxicity detection, CRM data grounding, audit logging, configurable guardrails, and contractual zero-data-retention agreements with third-party model providers.
Evaluation Notes: Comprehensive trust pipeline respecting granular Salesforce role-based permissions and data residency.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce actions can require explicit user confirmation before execution. Additionally, native Omni-Channel routing and Agent Script escalation routines support seamless transfer of unresolved interactions to human service representatives with full conversation context.
Evaluation Notes: Enforces pre-action user confirmations and transparent context handover during human escalation.

Evidence Summary: Agentforce Observability delivers Session Tracing data models, step-by-step reasoning logs, topic quality scores, deflection/escalation analytics, and Agentforce Testing Center evaluation scores, queryable via Data Cloud and visualized in Tableau.
Evaluation Notes: Provides operational trace and source citation transparency; not formal model-feature attribution or causal explainability.

Evidence Summary: Provides out-of-the-box domain-specific agents mapping directly to CRM and business operations, including Agentforce Service Agent, Sales Development Representative (SDR), Sales Coach, Commerce Agent, and Campaign Optimizer across sales, marketing, service, finance, and healthcare.
Evaluation Notes: Deep domain integration across Salesforce clouds and extensive cross-industry operational workflows.

Evidence Summary: A Forrester Total Economic Impact study demonstrated a 396% three-year ROI, 35% case deflection, 50% handling time reduction, and payback in under 12 months. Salesforce's internal deployment achieved a 40% reduction in qualification time and $20M in pipeline growth.
Evaluation Notes: Forrester study reflects independent composite financial modeling; internal deployment metrics are vendor-reported.

Evidence Summary: Built on Salesforce Hyperforce public cloud infrastructure and Data Cloud, Agentforce provides elastic compute scaling, global multi-region availability, and consumption-based scaling across channels (proven across >100k website and >2M Salesforce Help conversations).
Evaluation Notes: Native Hyperforce deployment supports global hyperscaler infrastructure and enterprise-scale concurrency.

Evidence Summary: Now Assist AI agents autonomously triage incoming service requests, execute multi-step diagnostic investigations, and remediate incidents end-to-end without manual intervention. Self-executing agentic workflows can be triggered automatically (via schedule, system events, or user intent) to analyze context, use configured tools, and execute actions across workflows and enterprise records.
Evaluation Notes: Operates autonomously across ITSM, CSM, and HRSD workflows without requiring manual invocation.

Evidence Summary: AI agents feature episodic memory learning, converting execution outcomes, past failures, and fixes into experience applied to future tasks. Now Assist Analytics, skill evaluation tools, and user feedback metrics (thumbs up/down) in the Now Assist Admin Console track acceptance rates to iteratively refine skills and prompts.
Evaluation Notes: Combines episodic outcome-based learning loops with administrator-guided prompt/skill evaluation and refinement.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow provides long-term semantic memory that retains user-specific facts across interactions, while AI Agent Orchestrator and Now Assist maintain short-term session memory during execution. Context is assembled by combining dialogue history with grounding from the ServiceNow Configuration Management Database (CMDB), user profiles, and active records.
Evaluation Notes: Combines short-term workflow tracking with persistent long-term semantic user memory and CMDB grounding.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow's AI Agent Orchestrator plans and coordinates tasks across AI agents, while individual agents use domain-tuned Now LLM reasoning engines, prompt-chaining, record context, searchable CMDB data, knowledge articles, and LLM-generated next-best actions to analyze unstructured incident logs, set intermediate goals, and execute remediation subflows.
Evaluation Notes: Supports dynamic reasoning and execution across structured CMDB data, business logic, and unstructured knowledge content.

Evidence Summary: Agentic workflows coordinate multi-step, cross-departmental actions using Flow Designer, Process Automation Designer, Playbooks, and the AI Agent Orchestrator. Workflows leverage triggers, tools, modular action blocks, and prebuilt agentic flow templates that can execute on a schedule, on demand, or in response to system events.
Evaluation Notes: Provides visual drag-and-drop orchestration templates alongside automatic trigger activation and AI-driven control flow.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Studio, Now Assist Skill Kit, and Creator Studio provide guided low-code/no-code visual builders to define agent roles, instructions, tools, memory, and access channels. The platform also supports natural-language agent creation in its Prime tier and prompt-based skill authoring.
Evaluation Notes: Enables citizen and pro developers to build and configure custom agents and skills visually or via natural language.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Studio provides guided setup for roles, triggers, channels, and memory, while AI Agent Advisor proposes or generates agents from instance data. Now Assist for Creator adds App Generation, Flow Generation from text prompts, Code Generation in Studio/VS Code, and Automated Testing Framework (ATF) support.
Evaluation Notes: Comprehensive developer tooling combining generative coding, automated flow drafting, and automated testing.

Evidence Summary: The ServiceNow AI Platform and Generative AI Controller support the proprietary Now LLM Service as well as third-party model providers including Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Cloud (Gemini), AWS (Claude), OpenAI, and IBM watsonx. Model selection can be assigned per skill or use case.
Evaluation Notes: Out-of-the-box model support varies across specific prebuilt skills and agentic workflows.

Evidence Summary: AI Agent Orchestrator coordinates multiple specialized domain agents (such as IT Service Desk, Case Triage, and Security Operations agents), managing task sequencing, context sharing, handoffs, and delegation across complex enterprise workflows.
Evaluation Notes: Multi-agent architecture enables collaboration and task delegation across IT, HR, and customer service domains.

Evidence Summary: Built on a multi-instance architecture with data segregation across global datacenters, the platform supports multi-tenant cloud instances, dedicated private sovereign clouds, FedRAMP High / DoD IL5 environments, and hybrid deployments managed via standard lifecycle and change review processes.
Evaluation Notes: Supports managed enterprise cloud and government/sovereign cloud instances; does not support arbitrary self-hosted runtime deployment.

Evidence Summary: Agents integrate with enterprise systems via Integration Hub (hundreds of prebuilt spokes), REST/SOAP APIs, OpenAPI imports, RPA Hub connectors, and record operations. The MCP Client enables agents to connect to external MCP servers, while the MCP Server Console exposes ServiceNow functionality to external AI applications.
Evaluation Notes: Supports bi-directional synchronous/asynchronous API execution and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling.

Evidence Summary: Security is enforced through platform ACLs, role-based access control (RBAC), AI-user identities, role masking, and runtime guardrails. Sensitive Data Handler detects and masks PII before sending prompts, and AI Control Tower provides centralized asset governance, compliance oversight, and lifecycle management.
Evaluation Notes: Enterprise-grade governance combining inline PII masking, identity segregation, and compliance auditing.

Evidence Summary: AI agents support supervised execution mode, pausing for user input, answering questions, or requiring human approval before critical tools execute. Workflows also support guided approvals, editable AI draft responses (e.g., ticket updates, emails), and seamless handoffs to live human service agents.
Evaluation Notes: Enforces pre-action human approvals for sensitive actions and seamless handoffs preserving context.

Evidence Summary: ServiceNow provides historical workflow run traces, step-level processing messages, AI Agent Analytics (usage, efficiency, token consumption, error rates), Generative AI Controller execution logs, and AI Control Tower for centralized oversight of agent activity and assets.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers comprehensive operational tracing and telemetry; this is not formal model-feature attribution or causal explainability.

Evidence Summary: Purpose-built agentic workflows and pre-trained models cover IT Service Management (ITSM), Customer Service Management (CSM), HR Service Delivery (HRSD), Field Service Management (FSM), and Security Operations (SecOps) for tasks like incident triage, resolution planning, and task classification.
Evaluation Notes: Deep vertical workflows mapping directly to standard enterprise business processes and departments.

Evidence Summary: A commissioned Forrester TEI study demonstrated up to 400% ROI over three years, accelerated incident resolution, and significant deflection. ServiceNow's internal deployment achieved 410,000 hours saved annually, $17.7M in cost avoidance, and 2.3M employee hours saved in 2025 (with 89% self-service resolution).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates strong financial and operational ROI; vendor-reported metrics combine AI agents with broader platform AI capabilities.

Evidence Summary: Built on ServiceNow's Advanced High Availability multi-instance architecture and RaptorDB high-throughput data store, the platform scales globally across datacenters to handle millions of workflow transactions, petabyte-scale data, and high-concurrency enterprise sessions.
Evaluation Notes: Proven high-availability enterprise scalability across global multi-instance datacenter infrastructure.

Evidence Summary: Signzy's Agentic CKYC Platform and Intelligent Process Automation (IPA) engine automate CKYC search, data validation, correction, image optimization, sensitive ID masking, and straight-through processing (STP) for customer onboarding and risk assessment without manual intervention when pre-set validation rules are met.
Evaluation Notes: Focuses on autonomous execution within regulatory identity verification, CKYC/CERSAI submission, and compliance rule domains.

Evidence Summary: The platform monitors model drift and applies ongoing risk scoring and rule calibration to optimize compliance, fraud detection, and transaction monitoring algorithms over time.
Evaluation Notes: Focuses on operational model performance monitoring and rule calibration; no official evidence of autonomous continual self-training or parameter adaptation from live interactions.

Evidence Summary: The Orchestrator persists application state, customer data, and API response payloads at journey checkpoints using unique customer/journey identifiers, maintaining back-office audit trails and session context across multi-step flows and transaction monitoring streams.
Evaluation Notes: Manages session state and lifecycle audit records; public documentation does not establish a general-purpose, persistent agent conversational memory service.

Evidence Summary: The platform utilizes an AI-based Rule and Decision Engine capable of evaluating up to 7 levels of conditional rules and risk scoring simultaneously for de-duplication, name screening/grading, fraud detection, and verification pathways.
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates automated multi-level deterministic and ML-driven decision logic rather than open-ended LLM chain-of-thought planning.

Evidence Summary: Signzy's No-Code API Orchestrator (NCO / Signzy GO) supports multi-stage journeys with drag-and-drop workflow configuration, conditional routing, API sequencing (sequential or parallel), checkpoints, and customized verification, validation, AI, and bank-specific business rules.
Evaluation Notes: Features visual drag-and-drop workflow authoring for complex, cross-channel onboarding and verification journeys.

Evidence Summary: Signzy GO provides a drag-and-drop no-code graphical platform enabling business and compliance teams to design onboarding journeys, set up multi-level decision rules, configure API sequencing, and integrate modular verification components without writing code.
Evaluation Notes: Confirms visual, no-code workflow and journey creation; does not establish an open-ended general-purpose agent builder.

Evidence Summary: Signzy provides an API Self-Service Portal featuring a secure sandbox environment, plug-and-play REST APIs, credential management, comprehensive documentation, pre-built frontend widgets, and no-code API onboarding tools.
Evaluation Notes: Streamlines integration and testing through self-service sandboxes, prebuilt widgets, and reusable modular components.

Evidence Summary: Not Publicly Evaluated.
Evaluation Notes: Signzy utilizes proprietary AI/ML, OCR, and computer vision models for verification; no public documentation exists for general foundation model switching or BYOLLM frameworks.

Evidence Summary: Not Publicly Evaluated.
Evaluation Notes: No sufficient official public documentation was found demonstrating autonomous multi-agent collaboration, delegation frameworks, or inter-agent protocols.

Evidence Summary: Signzy provides cloud SaaS delivery, preproduction/production HTTPS API environments, and cloud-native hosting with support for regional data localization and data residency compliance across global jurisdictions.
Evaluation Notes: Supports hosted cloud-native API access and jurisdiction-specific residency; broad on-premises or customer-managed self-hosting is not sufficiently documented.

Evidence Summary: Signzy offers an aggregated marketplace of over 200–240 REST API microservices, embeddable widgets, and a no-code API Orchestrator that handles data mapping, transformations, sequencing, retries, rate limiting, and webhooks across core banking and partner systems (e.g., India Stack, biometrics, databases).
Evaluation Notes: Comprehensive API coverage for identity verification, document extraction, AML/KYC checks, and external system connectivity.

Evidence Summary: Certified ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 compliant, supporting 256-bit encryption (at rest and in transit), HTTPS, mTLS, OAuth 2.0, API key authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), 24/7 security monitoring, and privacy audit trails.
Evaluation Notes: Strict adherence to financial-grade security, enterprise access management, and global regulatory compliance standards.

Evidence Summary: Integrates human-in-the-loop workflows across products, including a back-office case management console, role-based escalation queues for ambiguous cases, assisted Video KYC (V-CIP) with human verification, and manual review of probable face matches before CKYC submission.
Evaluation Notes: Enables explicit operator review and manual sign-off on flagged, ambiguous, or high-risk verification cases.

Evidence Summary: Provides operational traceability through back-office activity logs, API consumption statistics, transaction-level rule evaluation status breakdowns (violations, evaluation timings), MIS reporting, and Video KYC call analytics dashboards.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers robust operational logging, status tracking, and audit trails; formal AI reasoning explainability is not publicly documented.

Evidence Summary: Purpose-built for financial services, banking, NBFCs, fintech, insurance, lending, wealth management, and crypto due diligence across 150+ countries, with specialized workflows for KYC, KYB, AML, CKYC, and V-CIP.
Evaluation Notes: Deep domain specializations mapped directly to global identity verification and regulatory compliance frameworks.

Evidence Summary: Implementations deliver substantial operational gains, including a 90% reduction in turnaround time, a 70% decrease in manual reviews, a 75% drop in operational costs, a 66% reduction in customer drop-off, a 3x increase in successful onboardings, and deployment in 3–4 weeks.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Strong customer and platform performance metrics; figures are vendor- and customer-reported rather than independently audited ROI studies.

Evidence Summary: Designed for high-throughput enterprise scale, supporting over 1 million queries per hour, more than 10 million monthly onboardings/verifications at a 99% success rate, and over 300,000 monthly Video KYC calls for major banking clients.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Proven high-concurrency scalability in Tier-1 banking and fintech production deployments.

Evidence Summary: Writer AI agents autonomously execute end-to-end task pipelines—evaluating user inputs, determining when and how to select tools, executing custom Python scripts, querying Knowledge Graphs, and calling external APIs without manual intervention. Deployed no-code agents can also serve as reusable tools for other applications.
Evaluation Notes: Built on Agent Builder Blueprints, tool-calling execution blocks, and state execution engines.

Evidence Summary: The platform supports systematic prompt evaluation, activity log reviews, and continuous accuracy benchmarking against standard frameworks (e.g., Stanford HELM, MMLU) across Palmyra models to guide iterative refinement.
Evaluation Notes: Focuses on prompt evaluation and benchmark scoring; no official documentation found demonstrating autonomous continual learning or runtime model-parameter retraining.

Evidence Summary: Writer provides multi-turn session state management shared across components, persistent key-value storage across blueprint steps, and graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Knowledge Graph) for persisting and retrieving semantic contextual data across agent sessions.
Evaluation Notes: Agent state is session-scoped, while persistent storage and Knowledge Graph enable multi-session data persistence.

Evidence Summary: Writer agents use reasoning decomposition to break down complex queries into subquestions, evaluating structured intermediate logic via Palmyra models and conditional decision blocks. Tool Calling blocks enable agents to extract parameters, sequence actions, and apply ReAct-style iterative reasoning.
Evaluation Notes: Supports structured step decomposition, parameter extraction, and intermediate reasoning paths.

Evidence Summary: Agent Builder Blueprints provide visual and programmatic workflow orchestration using modular drag-and-drop blocks for loops, conditional if-else branching, RAG, text generation, classification, tool calling, state management, and custom enterprise workflows across people and systems.
Evaluation Notes: Blueprints define execution logic, routing, error handling, and cross-system orchestration (documented in Beta).

Evidence Summary: Writer provides both a No-Code Builder for prompt-based agent creation (defining inputs, instructions, and outputs) and a low-code visual Agent Builder featuring drag-and-drop blueprint canvases for configuring workflows, tools, RAG, and state.
Evaluation Notes: Enables technical and non-technical users to design logic and interfaces visually (Agent Builder noted in Beta).

Evidence Summary: Writer provides prebuilt agent templates, visual debuggers, local development sync, quickstart workflows, custom Python extension blocks, Docker-based local/cloud workflows, and official REST/Python/JS SDKs.
Evaluation Notes: Supports end-to-end development without requiring custom boilerplate application code.

Evidence Summary: Writer AI Studio supports its proprietary Palmyra foundation models (including Palmyra X5, Med, and Fin) alongside external models from AWS Bedrock, Microsoft Azure, and NVIDIA NIM, selectable via unified model settings and API parameters.
Evaluation Notes: External model support is available on Enterprise plans; provider and regional availability varies.

Evidence Summary: Writer Agent Builder supports multi-agent architectures by enabling agents to invoke, route tasks to, exchange state with, and be chained to other Writer-built agents and deployed no-code tools across shared enterprise workflows.
Evaluation Notes: Agents orchestrate work across multiple sub-agents, external systems, and reusable tool agents.

Evidence Summary: Writer supports deployment to Writer Cloud (multi-tenant SaaS), dedicated private clouds, multi-cloud setups (AWS, Azure), and self-contained Docker containers running on cloud platforms, on-premises servers, or local machines via Writer Framework.
Evaluation Notes: Docker-based containerization enables portable deployment across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises infrastructure.

Evidence Summary: Agents integrate with enterprise systems via Tool Calling blocks, REST APIs, developer SDKs, prebuilt integration blocks (e.g., PDF parsing, web search), and an MCP gateway offering prebuilt and custom connectors with configurable authentication and permissions.
Evaluation Notes: Native MCP gateway and tool calling blocks enable secure bi-directional connections to enterprise APIs and data stores.

Evidence Summary: Writer maintains SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27701/42001, and HIPAA compliance, enforcing RBAC, SSO/MFA, tenant data isolation, connector permissions, PII/content guardrails, and contractual zero customer data training policies.
Evaluation Notes: Enterprise-grade security framework with inline guardrails and strict zero-retention guarantees.

Evidence Summary: Writer agents support human review checkpoints, guided pagination interfaces, and approval-gated staging workflows (e.g., Palmyra X5 content generation and publishing approvals) before executing external operations.
Evaluation Notes: Documented approval workflows allow manual review checkpoints before publishing or updating external systems.

Evidence Summary: AI Studio provides session logs, performance metrics, event logs, execution state inspection, token usage, cost analytics, and OpenTelemetry exports, while chat interfaces offer step decomposition and direct Knowledge Graph source citations.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers operational tracing, latency/cost telemetry, and source citations; not formal model-feature attribution.

Evidence Summary: Provides domain-specialized foundation models (Palmyra-Med for healthcare/life sciences, Palmyra-Fin for financial services) and prebuilt agent libraries spanning finance, healthcare, legal, retail, marketing, sales, HR, and customer support.
Evaluation Notes: Purpose-built models and workflow templates fine-tuned on regulated industry terminology and schemas.

Evidence Summary: A Forrester TEI study reported 333% ROI, $12.02M NPV over 3 years, and payback under 6 months. Customer implementations show Qualcomm saving ~2,400 hours/month, Salesforce reporting a 20% productivity boost, and rapid deployment of custom workflows within days.
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates quantifiable productivity and financial outcomes; Forrester study was commissioned by Writer and metrics are customer-reported.

Evidence Summary: Scalable architecture leverages Knowledge Graph Retrieval Aware Compression (RAC) to index enterprise datasets, supporting up to 1M token context windows on Palmyra X5, with proven enterprise adoption across thousands of enterprise users (e.g., 3,000+ Salesforce employees).
Evaluation Notes: High-capacity context processing paired with horizontally scalable cloud and container runtimes.
